I can see the next eight weekends, from 23 October to 13 December. The most room is on the weekends of the 24th, the 14th and the 28th. Long weekends and school holidays fill early. Name a date, like "the 21st", and I will check it.
Happy to start that. Tell me the weekend and how many are coming, and Jo will confirm by text. Nothing is held until she does. You can also text her on 0491 570 158.

Ironbark is from $265 a night, Bottlebrush from $320 and Spotted Gum from $410. Weekends are a two night minimum. Linen, firewood and a bag of kindling are in the price. A 30 percent deposit holds your dates.

Ironbark sleeps two and is the quiet one on the ridge. Bottlebrush sleeps four, down by the creek. Spotted Gum sleeps six, with two bedrooms, and is the one for families. Kids are welcome. Cots and a high chair are on request.

Power is solar, enough for lights, the fridge and phone charging. Water is rainwater from tanks, with hot showers on gas. The toilets are composting and cleaner than you would guess. Bring a hair dryer if you like, then leave it in the bag.
Every cabin has a wood heater and the firewood is supplied. Spotted Gum also has a firepit out the front. Winter nights drop low in the gully, so the heater and the wool blankets get a workout.

There is no wifi and mobile reception is patchy. You get a bar or two on the ridge near Ironbark and almost nothing down at the creek. That is more or less the idea. Jo keeps one landline-style number for emergencies, written on the fridge.

We are near Rathdowney, in the Scenic Rim, under Mount Barney. The last stretch is gravel, and an ordinary car manages it when it is dry. The street address and gate code come with your confirmation, not on the website.

Check in is from 3pm and check out is by 10am. Arriving after dark is fine, the track has reflectors and Jo leaves a lantern lit. Bring your own food. Each cabin has a gas cooktop, a fridge, pots and pans, and a coffee plunger.
Dogs are welcome at Bottlebrush and Spotted Gum by arrangement, so ask Jo first. They stay on a lead near the creek because of the wildlife. No pets in Ironbark.

Change or cancel up to 14 days out and the deposit becomes credit for another weekend. A wet weekend here is no hardship, with a tin roof and a heater. If water cuts the track, Jo moves your dates at no charge.

Mostly nothing, on purpose. There is a creek track, a swimming hole when the water is up, and the star paddock after dark. Walks in the national park are a drive away, and Jo can point you to a good trailhead.
